data.title: Human-in-the-loop
data.tagline: Pausing an AI workflow before a critical decision or high-risk action so a person can review, approve, reject, or correct it
data.learningOutcome: You can identify where a workflow needs a human decision and state what the person must see and how approval or rejection affects the run.
data.description: A travel agent may search and compare flights automatically, but before payment it should show the dates, passenger, total, and change rules and wait for approval. Human-in-the-loop adds decision points where they matter rather than making a person watch every step.

learning.assumes: You know an AI agent can call tools and run a multi-step task.
learning.outcome: You can identify where a workflow needs a human decision and state what the person must see and how approval or rejection affects the run.

explanation.title: Pause before the action
explanation.text: Search and comparison can run automatically. Charging, ticketing, publishing, or deletion must be blocked before the high-risk action occurs.

explanation.title: Show enough information to decide
explanation.text: An approval cannot be only “continue?” The interface should show the object, scope, cost, rules, and expected consequence.

explanation.title: Return the decision to the same run
explanation.text: Approval resumes from the pause, rejection stops it, and corrections return with human feedback without restarting the whole task.

data.boundary: A guardrail can block automatically by rule; human-in-the-loop gives a key judgment to a person. Auth decides who has permission, while HITL decides when a human decision is required. The term is also used in data labeling and training; this page focuses on approval and correction during an agent run.

lessonPractice.title: A travel agent has found a suitable flight and is about to ticket it with a saved payment method. Where should human-in-the-loop approval occur?

options.label: Pause before charging and ticketing, show the dates, passenger, total, and change rules, then continue only after approval
options.feedback: Correct. The pause occurs before the irreversible action and gives the person enough information to approve, reject, or request a change.

options.label: Charge and issue the ticket automatically, then ask the user to review the order
options.feedback: The high-risk action has already happened, so the review cannot provide preventive control.

options.label: Require approval for every flight search, including read-only comparisons
options.feedback: Human-in-the-loop does not mean approving every step. Low-risk, reversible searches can remain automatic.

data.agentPrompt: You may search and compare weekend flights from Shanghai to Tokyo automatically, but pause before payment and ticketing. Show the round-trip dates, passenger, total with taxes, baggage, and change rules. Continue only after my explicit approval, and stop if I reject or the information changes.
